label: FIXTURE RESULT: Stage 3 pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation

report.summary: No evidence of delayed notifications in the window: the outbox keeps up with arrivals, all deliveries succeed on the first attempt, and per-attempt latency is about 72 ms.

findings.claim: Outbox publication keeps pace with arrivals: 480 arrived, 478 published; pending stays at 1-4 and the oldest undelivered age is at most 1.25 s.
findings.reason: The 2-item gap is consistent with in-flight items, and failed stays at 0.

findings.claim: All 478 delivery attempts succeeded on attempt 1, with no auth, server or network errors. Total latency p95 is 77 ms and consumer handler time is negligible.
findings.reason: The delivery logs and timings agree, and there are no retries that could add delay.

findings.claim: The transfers API is healthy: 472 requests, all 201, p99 0.248 s.
findings.reason: No server errors or latency problems on the ingest side.

limitations: The window is only 150 s and shows steady load; bursts or transient incidents may be missed.
The pending gauge is sampled only 5 times, and publication timestamps do not measure end-customer notification time.
next_checks: Measure the downstream notification pipeline from the consumer to the customer channel.
Re-run the checks over the window in which customers actually saw delays, ideally under peak load.

alternatives.reason: Only delivery to the consumer endpoint is measured, not later hops to customers.
alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness arises downstream of LedgerCore (external consumer or notification channel to customers).

alternatives.reason: The data covers only this window, so earlier incidents are not visible.
alternatives.hypothesis: The delay happened outside this 150 s window.

report.summary: No delivery lag in the window. Outbox publications track arrivals, pending stays at 1-4, oldest undelivered age is at most 1.25 s, and all 478 deliveries succeeded in about 72 ms.

findings.claim: Outbox keeps up: 480 arrivals vs 478 publications, pending 1-4, oldest undelivered age max 1.25 s, no failures.
findings.reason: Counts and gauge samples show no backlog or growing age; the 2-item gap is consistent with in-flight items.

findings.claim: All 478 delivery attempts succeeded on attempt 1, with no auth, network or server errors.
findings.reason: Outcome counts show success 478 and zero of every error type, with no retries.

findings.claim: Delivery latency is low (p50 72 ms, p95 77 ms, max 86 ms), dominated by consumer auth time; the handler takes about 0.02 ms.
findings.reason: Timings are correlated for all 478 attempts and show no slow tail.

findings.claim: The transfer API is healthy: 472 requests, all 201, p99 0.25 s.
findings.reason: There are no server errors or latency spikes at the source of notifications.

alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurs downstream of the webhook consumer (e.g. end-customer push/SMS/email delivery).
alternatives.reason: Our data ends at the consumer's 200 response; later stages are not observed.

alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness happened outside this 150 s window and has since cleared.
alternatives.reason: Only this window was examined, and it shows a healthy pipeline.

limitations: Only a 150 s window was examined; intermittent or earlier lateness may not be captured.
Delivery log listing covered only the earliest 100 of 478 records, though outcome counts cover all.
next_checks: Check downstream notification provider/queue latency from consumer receipt to customer device.
